chapter_title: Concerning the Purification of these Four Elements

fills.notes: Balances the impersonal, definitional style of the substrate: the elements themselves are the purifying agents/subjects, not merely objects of purification.

The correspondential pivot is the first crisis: perception/consent to mixture. The oldest layer typically speaks of “mingling” (mixture) as the operative event that introduces Darkness into the elements’ vessels.
What is stripped off becomes manifest in an outward plane and then threatens the body; “displayed in a visible form” matches correspondential logic (pollution becomes externalized in ultimates).

After “voices of the winds of shame,” the next discharge is the bodily/spiritual effect of shame: an agitated vibration in ultimates. “Trembling” fits the emission-chain pattern (substance → affect → bodily symptom).

The tear (moisture of grief/shame) culminates the chain as a “crown,” i.e., the completion/encirclement of the twelve emissions into a single total effect. This is a substrate way of marking the last as the summation of the series.
Matches the technical, impersonal register already present (“management of this soul food”), introducing the doctrine of ordered administration rather than exhortation.
The four elements are said earlier to be purifiers; here they “shall purify” what is gathered inside. Keeps the inside→outside correspondential motion (gathered particles are worked upon).

After establishment in the living image (new man), the purified elements ‘live’ in their proper discrete degrees/regions. “Aeons” preserves the cosmological/topological idiom of the oldest layer (proper realms), without later pastoral coloring.

assessment: Most gaps are recoverable by the emission-chain logic (each element disgorges a corresponding pollution leading to a bodily/affective ultimate) and by the administrative/purificatory role of the four elements. Two restorations remain tentative: ¶6’s final emission (the bodily effect of shame) and ¶7’s summarizing term for the twelfth (rendered as “crown” to mark completion of the series).
